# Exergy

> Exergy (Exergy LLC, Denver, CO) finds the useful work hiding in a building's energy and in a company's operations, and cuts the waste. The name is the thermodynamic term for the share of energy that can still do useful work. The lead business is commercial consulting for building-integrated bitcoin mining: building energy systems powered by bitcoin miners. Heat recovery and solar monetization are separate value streams. Integration is hydronic or forced air. Exergy sells no hardware. Residential work is an application-only alpha pilot, not the headline. Exergy is open-source first and aligned with the 256 Foundation open mining stack. Founder and CEO Tyler Stevens is president of the 256 Foundation board.

Commercial work is phased, and each phase is its own agreement. A client can stop after any phase. Phase 0 is a free feasibility check from about twelve months of utility bills. Phase 1 is an Exergy Audit (energy, heat, and bitcoin economics, with one to three options and an estimated budget). Phase 2 is engineering coordination alongside the architect, MEP engineer, and general contractor. Phase 3 is procurement support and commissioning. Phase 4, monitoring and warranty, is optional. Fees are scoped per project and are not published.

Other services: manufacturer and market-entry advisory (paid discovery sprint, then a fixed-fee monthly pilot) for companies building miners, heaters, boilers, or water heaters; operations optimization for energy-adjacent small businesses (HVAC and solar installers, property managers, mining operators); and a residential pilot (guided remote anywhere in the US, done with Exergy's crew within about 100 miles of Denver). Pilot systems are tied together with an open-source control hub Exergy installs, and monitored with Exergy Relay (a 5% hashrate split). Neither is for sale.
